correctness.rationale: A direct Bernoulli sawtooth identity holds a.e. Each Fourier mode of every centered F_j is proportional to W_j(n), which is nonnegative for d not dividing n and nonpositive for d dividing n. Parseval proves all nonnegative pair covariances; n=d gives strict positivity for noncentral pairs because both index divisors of d imply j=d/2. The algebraic gcd formula follows from the classical exact Bernoulli integral. Exact direct integration verified 7,139 integer-index pairs up to d=35. Limits: finite diagnostics do not prove all d; analytic proof does.

value.rationale: The precise two-index phase covariance is an intrinsic arithmetic invariant of Kummer carry functions, motivated by comparing binomial indices. It establishes a complete universal nonnegative sign law and a strict noncentral boundary, not an arbitrary finite slice or a trivial equality: the signed gcd expression does not visibly have fixed sign. It gives the exact bivariate law for each index pair, while carefully declining to infer higher-order or integer-sampled dependence.
